hook.title: A notebook of how good each turn is
hook.text: Learning to drive in a new city, you keep a **notebook**: for every junction and every possible turn, a number for “how good is it to turn this way?”. Each time you try a turn you see the immediate result and peek at the best number written for the *next* junction, then you **nudge** your old number a little toward “result + discounted best-next”. Occasionally you try a random turn (**ε-greedy**) so every page of the notebook keeps getting updates. Over time the notebook converges to the optimal guide $Q^*$ — even though you didn't always drive optimally.
hook.recall: Remember the notebook: nudge each entry toward $r+\gamma\max Q(s',\cdot)$ by a fraction $\alpha$ of the error; explore occasionally so every entry keeps being updated; the greedy turn from the notebook is $\arg\max_aQ(s,a)$.

explore.intro: A 4×4 grid with +10 at the bottom-right (terminal), −1 per move. Watch the Q-table fill in.
tasks: Press *1 step* a few times and read the update line. What changes in the table?
Run 3000 steps with $\varepsilon=0$ then with $\varepsilon=0.2$. Which explores the whole grid?
explore.takeaway: $Q(s_t,a_t)\leftarrow Q(s_t,a_t)+\alpha[r+\gamma\max_{a'}Q(s_{t+1},a')-Q(s_t,a_t)]$. Converges if all pairs keep being updated.

items: Randomly initialise $Q(s_t,a_t)$ for all state–action pairs
Initialise the starting state $s_t$ of the episode
Choose $a_t$ from a policy derived from $Q$ (e.g. ε-greedy)
build.explanation: Repeat for each step until $s_t$ is terminal and for each episode.

questions.prompt: If $Q^*$ is known, the optimal action in state $s$ is:
For correct convergence of tabular Q-learning, the only requirement mentioned is:
options: All state–action pairs continue to be updated
A Q-table stores a value for each state–action pair
ε-greedy is an example of a policy derived from $Q$
Q-learning converges to $Q^*$ only if the data is collected by the optimal policy
Tabular Q-learning needs finite state and action spaces
questions.explanation: “No matter which policy is used to collect the state and action pairs”: it is off-policy.

questions.prompt: *“Initialise $Q$ to zeros and always act greedily; every pair will be updated.”* What’s wrong?
options: A purely greedy agent may never try some actions, so some pairs stop being updated; use exploration (e.g. ε-greedy)
Q must start random and negative
questions.explanation: If you always take the first turn that looks good you never write the rest of the notebook.
